The Charter also outlined the establishment of a Security Council, the General Assembly, and the International Court of Justice.

The signing of the Charter was followed by the ratification of the United Nations’ International Declaration of Human Rights in 1948. This document laid out fundamental human rights that would serve as the basis for many international treaties, and the implementation of these rights within the UN’s own system of protection.

The United Nations has since grown to include 193 members and has had a considerable effect on global affairs. It has taken a leading role in addressing issues such as global poverty, inequality and the spread of HIV/AIDS, as well as tackling the threats posed by climate change and terrorism."

The four stages of natural selection are variation, heritability, selection, and adaptation. Variation occurs when individuals in a species have unique attributes. The basic principles of the theory of evolution, proposed by Charles Darwin, are that all life on Earth has descended from a common ancestor and that this evolution occurs over time via the process of natural selection. Natural selection is the process by which individuals who are better adapted to their environment are more likely to survive, reproduce, and pass on their traits to their offspring. This process leads to the formation of new species and allows for adaptation in a changing environment. \n\nIn addition, the theory of evolution explains how new genetic variations arise, how organisms acquire inherited traits, and how species diverge with time.
